Intercrop with onion, Bengal gram. Rotate with maize or sorghum. Needs dry climate at maturity.
Suitable for coastal regions. Once established, low input. Grows in poor soils. No intercrop recommended after 3rd year.
Intercrop with cocoa, pineapple, banana, or turmeric in early years. Regular irrigation increases yield.
Intercrop with black pepper or banana. Shade-loving intercrops like ginger also suit. Requires humid climate.
Grown in high-altitude Western Ghats. Requires shade and high rainfall. Very specific agro-climatic need.
Rotate with pulses or onion. Intercrop with coriander. Needs dry weather during fruit maturity.
Intercrop with pepper, banana, or cardamom. Needs shade, well-drained soil, and elevation (900–1500 m).
Intercrop with onion or coriander. Rotate with legumes or millets. Sensitive to water stress and pests.
Rotate with maize, groundnut, or green gram. Intercrop with coriander or garlic.
Intercrop with peas or garlic. Rotate with cereals or mustard. Requires cool climate.
Intercrop with turmeric, short vegetables. Needs good drainage and high humidity.
Suitable for dryland. Intercrop with legumes/vegetables in early 3–4 years.
High investment. Suitable for dry, frost-free regions. Sensitive to rainfall during flowering.
Intercrop with legumes or onion. Requires dry climate. Susceptible to bacterial blight.
Short-lived tree crop. Intercrop with short-term crops like green gram or coriander in initial months.
Intercrop with legumes or ginger. Requires acidic, well-drained soils. Suitable for coastal hills.
Suitable for homesteads. Needs well-drained soil. Intercropping not advised post establishment.
Rotate with maize or pulses. Intercrop with chilli or onion. Requires shade, rich organic matter.
Intercrop with banana or turmeric. Needs loamy soil and high organic matter.
